top_signals.title: Asia Needs $1 Trillion a Year to Secure Energy Supplies
top_signals.summary: Asia will need as much as $1 trillion annually in energy investment over the next 15 years to meet rising demand and reduce its exposure to supply disruptions, according to a McKinsey report released Thursday. That amounts to $15 trillion through 2040, with the Iran war exposing just how vulnerable the region remains to disruptions in oil and gas shipments through the Strait of Hormuz. McKinsey now expects Asian energy demand to reach 370 million terajoules by 2040, a 15% increase over its forecast from just a year ago. The region is expected to…

top_signals.title: Threats to financial system ‘on steroids’ after AI boom, FCA chief warns
top_signals.summary: The unchecked rise of artificial intelligence means the level of risk facing the financial system is currently “on steroids”, according to the boss of the Financial Conduct Authority, who warned that excessive “tick-box” rulemaking would fail to keep pace with increasingly complex threats. top_signals.title: Chile Copper Slump Deepens as Storms, Accidents Hit Aging Mines
top_signals.summary: Chile’s copper production will likely fall 8% to 9% this year, Finance Minister Jorge Quiroz said, worsening his outlook for a slump in the top-producing nation amid a string of deadly accidents and extreme weather.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Commodity repricing impacting inflation expectations and industrial supply chains.

top_signals.title: Braddick sets out her vision for banking watchdog with £2bn overhaul
top_signals.summary: Katharine Braddick has kicked off her revamp of the UK banking’s watchdog with a regulatory overhaul aiming to generate £2bn in savings for City firms. The Prudential Regulation Authority chief, who took the reins in July, told a City audience on Thursday evening the watchdog would focus on four key priorities of resilience, growth, innovation [...]

top_signals.title: Why Fossil Fuel Demand Can Rise Even as Clean Energy Wins Terrain
top_signals.summary: French historian Jean-Baptiste Fressoz has offered energy-transition skeptics an appealing historical argument. In More and More and More, he argues that humanity has never really moved from one energy source to another. Wood was joined by coal, coal by oil, oil by gas and all of them by renewables. Energy sources accumulate rather than replace one another. Global primary-energy charts make the argument look convincing. Fossil use remains near record levels after trillions in clean-energy investment. Biomass did not disappear when coal arrived,…

top_signals.title: Closed College Campus in Boston Suburb to Sell for $21M
top_signals.summary: Bloomberg's Elizabeth Rembert joins Scarlet Fu on "Bloomberg Real Yield." A Boston suburb’s housing authority is planning to buy the campus of Eastern Nazarene College, which closed last year, for $21 million. (Source: Bloomberg)
